name: Ramen-GRPO-Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid gated linear attention (Gated DeltaNet) in parallel with full GQA attention every 4th layer; 12 of 48 layers are full attention
notes: ADDED 2026-11-02. Ramen-GRPO: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct fine-tuned with GRPO on the same Japanese medical-MCQ RL setup as its sibling Ramen-CHORD (catalogued as ramen-chord-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct) by the Ramen Team, University of Tokyo / NEDO JPNP25006. Deterministic RL, not a merge or a quant: config.json matches the base field for field (2048 hidden, 48 layers, 512 experts, 10 per token, 262144 ctx, 12 full-attention layers of 48) and the repo ships full BF16 safetensors at 79,674,391,296 parameters, the base's rounded 80B label. ms-swift + Megatron-LM v3.9.3, apache-2.0. flops_per_token_active inherited from the base at 6.0e9 (2 x 3B active), overriding the generator's 6x-active default - the same systematic 3x disagreement flagged in PR #466. Recorded because the card prints a 'ベース' column and a 'this model' column in the SAME table on two exam benchmarks. Caveats the card states itself, carried into the rows: igakuqa win is +90.3 points on 1,122 items and McNemar p=0.349 (NOT significant); specialist_exam_test_v2 is +71.1 on 3,757 items, p=0.0013 (significant). The wins are small in absolute terms, and this is the same three-way method comparison (GRPO vs GSPO vs CHORD) reported from one base inside one project, so the three records are comparable to each other and to nothing else. The card also declares no clinical validation and no J-HealthBench/Do-Not-Answer/AnswerCarefully runs. Read it as a method datapoint, not a leaderboard entry.
